body.en: The Problem-Solving and Data Analysis domain asks you to interpret tables, graphs, and real-world contexts — no formula memorisation needed, but careful reading is essential.
A car travels 240 km in 3 hours. How long does it take to travel 400 km at the same speed? \[ \text{Speed}=\frac{240}{3}=80\ \text{km/h},\quad t=\frac{400}{80}=5\ \text{hours}. \]

Interpreting graphs

On the EST I, you may be given a scatterplot, bar chart, or two-way table and asked to read a value, find a percentage, or determine whether a conclusion is justified. Always identify the units on each axis before computing.

Ratio: compare two quantities, e.g. \(a:b\). Rate: ratio with different units (speed, price per unit). Percentage change: \(\dfrac{\text{new}-\text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100\%\). Proportion: two equal ratios \(\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}\). Weighted average: \(\bar{x} = \dfrac{\sum w_i x_i}{\sum w_i}\).

label.en: Worked example — Percentage increase and reverse

body.en:
A price increases by 20%, then decreases by 20%. Is the final price the same as the original?

Original = 100. After 20% increase: \(120\). After 20% decrease: \(120 \times 0.8 = 96\). No — it is 4% less than original.

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Ratios, Rates & Percentages

body.en:
• Percent Change Base Value: Always divide by the ORIGINAL quantity: \(\frac{\text{new} - \text{old}}{\text{old}} \times 100\%\). For example, if a price drops from $80 to $60, the percent decrease is \(\frac{20}{80} = 25\%\), NOT \(\frac{20}{60} = 33.3\%\).
  • Successive Percentage Multipliers: Never add or subtract percentages directly! A 30% markup followed by a 20% discount is \(1.30 \times 0.80 = 1.04\) (a net 4% increase), NOT \(30\% - 20\% = 10\%\).
  • Average Speed is NOT Average of Speeds: Average speed equals \(\frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}}\). If you travel 60 miles at 30 mph (2 hours) and return 60 miles at 60 mph (1 hour), your average speed is \(\frac{120}{3} = 40\text{ mph}\), NOT \(\frac{30+60}{2} = 45\text{ mph}\).
  • Square and Cubic Unit Conversions: When converting area and volume units, square or cube the conversion factor! \(1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm} \implies 1\text{ m}^2 = (100)^2 = 10,000\text{ cm}^2\) and \(1\text{ m}^3 = 1,000,000\text{ cm}^3\).

question.en: A car travels 240 km in 3 hours, then 180 km in 2 hours. Find the average speed for the whole journey.

solution.en: Total distance \(= 420\) km. Total time \(= 5\) h. Average speed \(= 420/5 = 84\) km/h.

question.en: A retailer purchases a watch from a wholesaler for $80. The retailer marks up the wholesale price by 40% for retail display, and later offers a 25% discount off the display price during a promotion. (a) What is the promotional selling price of the watch? (b) What is the retailer's net percent profit relative to the wholesale cost?

solution.en:
(a) Promotional selling price:

  • Marked-up display price: \[ 80 \times (1 + 0.40) = 80 \times 1.40 = \$112. \]
  • Promotional price after 25% discount: \[ 112 \times (1 - 0.25) = 112 \times 0.75 = \$84. \]

(b) Net profit percentage: Profit is \(84 - 80 = \$4\). The net percent profit relative to wholesale cost is: \[ \dfrac{4}{80} \times 100\% = 5\%. \] Notice that \(1.40 \times 0.75 = 1.05\) directly gives a 5% net gain.
